xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4757: Flaky e2e: pan-2355-mobile spec finds two 'Yes' buttons (strict mode violation) on main

plan.title: Flaky e2e: pan-2355-mobile spec finds two 'Yes' buttons (strict mode violation) on main
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: The pan-2355-mobile Playwright spec hard-codes the fixture question time to 2026-11-01T00:00Z. The Needs-you row header button renders formatRelativeTime(since), which reads 'yesterday' once the question is 24-47 hours old. Playwright's getByRole name match is a case-insensitive substring match, so first.getByRole('button', { name: 'Yes' }) at spec line 133 matched both the Yes option and the row header ('… yesterday'), a strict-mode violation. Every test-e2e run on main between 2026-11-02T00:00Z and 2026-11-03T00:00Z fails deterministically; the issue's duplicate-render and second-question hypotheses are ruled out.
narratives.Proposal: In one commit, change the Yes tap to { name: 'Yes', exact: true } and compute the PENDING fixture askedAt values from Date.now(), pinning pan-2355-ship to 25 hours ago (docs row 5 minutes later) so the header always reads 'yesterday'. The former date bomb becomes a permanent regression guard. Document the Playwright substring rule and relative-fixture-time rule in docs/TESTING.md and the codebase conventions map. No component changes.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No change to MobileNeedsYou.tsx, formatRelativeTime.ts, useDecisions.ts, or any file under src/dashboard/frontend/src/
- No .first(), .nth(), test retry, or retries config added to the spec
- No change to the Send, Conversations, Back, or other locators in the spec
- No sweep of other Playwright specs for missing exact: true
- No change to the CONVERSATIONS fixture dates
- No change to CI workflow files or playwright.config.ts

autoDecisions.summary: Root cause is the 'yesterday' relative-time text in the row header matching name: 'Yes' as a substring, not a duplicate render or a second question.
autoDecisions.rationale: Green run #12495 started 23h52m after the fixture askedAt ('23h ago'); red run #12496 started 24h37m after ('yesterday'). QuestionCard renders each option once and the fixture has one Yes/No question.

autoDecisions.summary: Use exact: true on the Yes locator instead of .first().
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue forbids a blind .first(); .first() would also tap the row header, which precedes the card in DOM order. exact: true targets the option by whole name.

autoDecisions.summary: Pin the ship fixture to 25 hours before the run so the header always reads 'yesterday'.
autoDecisions.rationale: Turns a one-day date bomb into a permanent regression guard and makes the fix verifiable on any date; 25h sits mid-band in the 24-48h 'yesterday' window.

autoDecisions.summary: Both spec edits land in a single item and commit.
autoDecisions.rationale: The fixture pin without exact: true makes the spec fail on every run, so the edits are not independently mergeable.

autoDecisions.summary: Leave the Send locator unchanged and do not sweep other specs.
autoDecisions.rationale: Nothing else in the ship card contains 'send'; the docs rule covers future specs and the issue scopes the fix to this spec.

items.title: Match the Yes option exactly and pin pan-2355-mobile fixture times to 25h ago

narrative.Action: Edit only src/dashboard/frontend/tests/pan-2355-mobile.spec.ts, following PRD WI-1 exactly. (1) Replace the PENDING array (search 'const PENDING = [', lines 48-51) with: a comment explaining the 'yesterday' collision (PAN-4757); `const SHIP_ASKED_AT = Date.now() - 25 * 60 * 60 * 1000;`; the ship row askedAt `new Date(SHIP_ASKED_AT).toISOString()`; the docs row askedAt `new Date(SHIP_ASKED_AT + 5 * 60 * 1000).toISOString()`. (2) Change line 133 to `await first.getByRole('button', { name: 'Yes', exact: true }).tap();`. Change no other line. Commit both edits in one commit with an `Item: spec-exact-yes` trailer. Verify with `npm run build` then `cd src/dashboard/frontend && npx playwright test tests/pan-2355-mobile.spec.ts`. Optional negative check (do not commit): with only edit (1) applied the spec fails with 'strict mode violation … resolved to 2 elements' at the Yes tap.
